changelog:
0.3.0

  • Adds the Shipping and Save & Resume modules, so three of the four DTF Studio snippets now live in the plugin.
  • Each module stands down independently while its own snippet is active, so you can deactivate them one at a time and check between each — no all-or-nothing cutover.
  • Shipping keeps the method ID btgsb_shipping, so your configured zone rates carry over. Save & Resume keeps the wp_btgsb_saves table, its AJAX actions and the nightly cron hook, so existing resume links still work.
  • The Frontend snippet (the builder UI) is unchanged and still runs from WPCode. It talks to the plugin through the same AJAX actions and nonce, so it keeps working either way.

0.2.0

  • Fixes the fatal in 0.1.0. That build kept the snippet's btgsb_* function names, so activating it while the DTF Studio snippet was still on caused a PHP redeclare and took the site down. Every function is now btdtf_ and every constant BTDTF_ — zero names in common, so a redeclare cannot happen in any activation order.
  • Nothing registers at load. Hooks wait for plugins_loaded priority 999, after WPCode has evaluated its snippets, and the plugin stands fully dormant (no menu, no AJAX, no order columns, no duplicate meta) if the old snippet is still active — with a notice explaining why.
  • Option names, order meta keys, AJAX actions, the nonce, page slugs and CSS classes are unchanged, so existing orders, saved settings and the DTF Studio Frontend snippet keep working untouched.
  • Same coexistence model as BT Portal: activate the plugin, verify it, then deactivate the snippet whenever you like.

0.1.0

  • Initial plugin release — the DTF Studio — Backend snippet moved into a real plugin with dashboard auto-updates, so fixes arrive as an Update button instead of a paste.
  • Every option name, AJAX action, meta key and function name is unchanged, so existing orders, settings and pricing tiers carry over untouched. Nothing to migrate.
  • Conflict guard: if the old WPCode snippet is still active the plugin stays inert and shows a notice, rather than fatally redeclaring its functions and white-screening the site.
  • Includes the Awaiting Items tracking flag — a badge and filter on the Orders list that never changes an order's WooCommerce status, so flagged orders cannot drop out of the list.
  • The four custom order statuses (Art Approved, Printing, Ready for Pickup, Shipped) and their two customer emails remain removed.
